title: Choose a cost-preserving level of abstraction
obstacle: The source counts a particular resource, but the proposed implementation creates extra obligations or omits costs required by that model.
procedure: Identify the stated resource, input measure, fixed parameters and charged operations. Consider an abstraction that expresses the actual algorithm at that level.
Where the proof crosses an encoding, compilation or simulation boundary, substitute the quantitative overhead of a proved connection into the requested bound.
A missing connection can be recorded as an obligation. A change to a frozen interface belongs with its owner.
verification: Check the model and the final rate, including uniform constants and encoding overhead, against the original statement.
positive_example: For polynomial evaluation charged by scalar additions and multiplications, count the actual operations of the evaluation algorithm directly.
negative_example: A polynomial-time simulation alone does not preserve a near-linear bound. Unit-cost scalar multiplication need not have constant bit cost.

evidence.note: General design guidance. Check its conditions in the current argument; no comparative performance claim.
